annotations.annotation_text: Page 376 opens Book 2, Chapter 3 ("The Tavern") during the Age of Heroes phase. This passage continues HCE behind the bar at his Chapelizod pub, the Norwegian Captain tale, the television broadcast, the twelve customers drinking and judging, featuring HCE, the Twelve Customers, Butt and Taff. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.

annotations.annotation_text: Dublin landmark "Clontarf" on page 376 ("The Tavern"): grounding the cosmic dream in physical Dublin during HCE behind the bar at his Chapelizod pub, the Norwegian Captain tale, the television broadcast, the twelve customers drinking and judging. Joyce transforms this real location into a universal archetypal site — simultaneously Eden, Waterloo, Calvary, and the Elysian Fields — within the Age of Heroes phase.
